Everyone’s going to say “a restaurant.” I’d make an ad for a locksmith. 🔑

I work nights as a security guard, and I know who people are frantically searching for on their phones at 3 a.m. It’s not a burger, it’s someone to get them back inside. Tradespeople like that make good money, but their ads are terrible or nonexistent, and nobody thinks of them.

My ad: 15 seconds. A door slams shut, the keys are still inside, it’s pouring rain. Then: “Door open in 20 minutes. Day or night.” with the locksmith’s name. I’d make it before ever contacting him and send it over for free. If he wants it without my watermark, he pays.

Tracing your real journey-from making wooden trash cans for under $2 an hour at 16, to having a friend steal your RC shop idea, getting rejected by your bank in 10 minutes, and still buying that business back to build an empire-is a far better story. People respect someone who survived real setbacks way more than generic money tips

I would suggest an ad for the website of a doctor’s office (background loop):
Concept: "Time for You"
Mood: bright, soft colors (white, light green or blue), natural daylight, slow camera movements. No sound, no on-screen text, seamless loop.
Scene sequence (approx. 20 seconds)
1. 0-4 sec: Arrival. Gentle sunrise look. The camera glides slowly through the entrance door of the practice. Light falls on a tidy reception area, with a plant in the foreground.
2. 4-9 sec: Welcome. A staff member smiles at an elderly patient at the front desk, both looking relaxed. A brief focus shift to their hands as they touch in greeting.
3. 9-14 sec: Listening. In the consultation room, the doctor and patient sit at eye level at a table, with no computer in the foreground. The doctor nods, listens, and takes notes calmly. The camera makes a subtle orbit around the scene.
4. 14-18 sec: Relief. Close-up: the patient exhales and smiles. Then a cut to a family leaving the practice, children and grandparents together in the autumn sun.
5. 18-20 sec: Loop transition. The camera pans back to the entrance door and softly dissolves into the opening scene, so the video plays endlessly.
